intro: At 02:17 local time, operators in the Central Control Room at Blackwood Regional Water Authority reported sudden level oscillations in raw water balancing tank T-101 and an intermittent freeze across SCADA HMI-01. Field operators confirmed physical water surging through the intake galleries despite SCADA displays indicating a calm, nominal baseline. As lead OT/ICS forensic investigator you are handed packet captures, historian exports, the safety controller image and, as the case unfolds, live access to the plant's engineering systems. Reconstruct a cascading, multi-stage attack - from the first leaked DNS query to a clean standby controller about to replicate poisoned numbers - and bring the plant back without letting it fail.

leaky-hop.open:
“Every session to the PLC comes from the proxy. One box in the DMZ, a thousand connections behind it. Attribution's impossible.”
“The SOC already closed it as unattributable.”
“Proxies lie about the source address. They don't lie about everything.”

The intruder tunnelled through an open proxy in the DMZ, so every TCP session to PLC-01 wears the proxy's face. But a proxy only relays the stream it carries - and before any of that traffic could flow, the attacker's own machine had to do a little housekeeping of its own.

The span capture from the window of the breach is in front of you. Somewhere in the noise, the real source spoke for itself.
leaky-hop.close:
“There,” you say. “Strip away everything the proxy relayed and one host still reached out on its own - the real source, named in the clear.”

“Sure it isn't another decoy?” Miller asks.

“Two independent places in the capture agree on the same address. That's our intruder.” The ghost has a face now. But the address was only the opening move - the historian insists the tank was calm all night, and the weir wall says otherwise.

impossible-levels.open:
"The historian swears T-101 held steady all night."
"Then why is the weir wall wet and the overflow sensors damp?"
"Because someone taught the HMI to lie. They can spoof a database. They can't spoof conservation of mass."

You pull the tank geometry, the P-101 discharge curve and the raw historian export: inflow, outflow, pump state and the level the HMI showed the operators. The logged outflow looks tidy. Too tidy - the pump is logged stopped while a discharge flow keeps appearing, just enough to make the numbers balance on paper.

Integrate the real physics and find the moment the displayed level became something the tank could never have held.
impossible-levels.close:
Line by line the true level pulls away from the HMI trace. While the display sat pinned at a comfortable five metres, the water climbed to within a breath of the High-High mark.

"Peak deviation," you announce, reading the number off your reconstruction. "That's how far the screen lied, in metres." The flag falls out of the gap between the water and the story the HMI told.

"So it really was filling," Miller says, pale. "Then why in God's name didn't the safety system trip the inlet?"

silent-safety.open:
"T-101 has triple redundant level transmitters. Two-out-of-three voting, SIL-2. Any two above High-High and emergency valve XV-101 fails closed. Hardwired."
"Two of them read 8.85 metres. XV-101 never moved."
"The hardware's fine. The logic was recompiled twenty minutes before the shift."

You pull the compiled safety image off the engineering workstation. Somewhere inside is a voting table, a Cause & Effect matrix, and a diagnostic path that should never suppress a real demand. Reverse it and find how two tripped sensors voted to do nothing - quietly, without raising the mismatch alarm that would have given the game away.
silent-safety.close:
"They didn't just weaken the vote - they gutted it," you say. "The A-and-C pair term is gone. Pin sensor B low and a genuine A+C demand simply never reaches the output. Then they wired a diagnostic override on word 0x7A4F that latches suppression without flagging a voter mismatch."

You lift the forced-bypass string straight out of the binary. The safety system went silent because someone paid off two of its three votes. All physical protection is gone - and the attacker still has a foothold.

ghost-rung.open:
"The workstation shows a clean ladder program."
"The PLC disagrees. Pull the online checksum."
"...it doesn't match the project on disk."

The attacker hid a rung the engineering software never renders. Below is the live panel: the ladder view the workstation draws, an I/O force table, a memory viewer, and the online/offline checksum diff. The mismatch is exactly the size of a data block that isn't supposed to exist.

Dump raw %DB99, reverse its small bytecode, and satisfy the trigger the hidden rung is waiting for. When it fires, the backdoor configuration will surface in memory for anyone who knows where to look.
ghost-rung.close:
The hidden rung wakes only when every condition lines up at once - the forced pump, the level above setpoint, the seven-second timer, the three pulses, the C3 word in %MW50. Hold them together and %MW200 onward blooms with ASCII that was never in the project file.

You read the backdoor config straight out of the PLC's memory. The ghost rung didn't exist until %DB99 said otherwise. Now you understand the implant - enough to replay the whole thing in a sandbox.

cascade-complete.open:
"We can't test recovery on live drinking-water plant."
"We don't have to. We rebuilt the attacker's console against a sandbox that runs T-101's physics in real time."

Replay the full chain: connect spoofing the real source, inhibit the SIS with the bypass word, arm the implant with the backdoor config, and drive the true level to its peak while the HMI smiles and shows nothing wrong. The history log even hides one pump step that the mass balance says is a lie.

Then comes the part nobody expected. The HMI locks. The screen shows pump P-2 steady ON - but the implant is pulsing it, tapping a message out through the one signal it still controls. Log the raw level current, watch the slope flip, and read what the pump is saying.
cascade-complete.close:
The P-2 lamp glows a steady, innocent green. The 4-20 mA level trace tells a different story: a fast stutter of rises and falls, mid-bit edges marching in lockstep. Manchester. You clock it out edge by edge and the bits fall into ASCII.

The pump spoke in Manchester while the screen smiled. You have the attacker's parting message - and, folded inside it, the recovery key. Just in time: upstairs, the primary PLC's watchdog just faulted.

hot-standby.when: Day 0 - 04:40 - Control Room, Failover In Progress
hot-standby.open:
"Primary watchdog just faulted. That's the implant's parting shot."
"Fail over to the hot standby - it runs clean firmware, no implant."
"It also syncs every data block from the primary every few seconds. Including recipe block DB10, which the attacker poisoned hours ago. When failover completes, the clean controller will faithfully run his numbers."

You have the recovery key and a live redundancy panel: primary and standby status, a sync countdown, a failover timer, a %DB10 hex editor and the tank. The poisoned REALs are word-swapped - CDAB instead of ABCD - so they read as plausible numbers in the wrong byte order. The editor shows you both.

Fix the setpoints on the primary before the next sync carries them across, let failover complete, and hold the tank steady.
hot-standby.close:
You rewrite the swapped words - HiHi back to 8.50, the pump bands and fill rate back to sane engineering values - with seconds to spare before the sync pulse. Failover completes onto the clean standby, and this time it replicates clean numbers. The tank holds flat for a full minute.

The panel clears and hands you the recovery token. You were exactly one sync ahead of the poison.

finale.title: Cascade Failure Averted - Plant Restored
finale.text:
"Water quality lab: nothing reached the municipal grid. Secondary containment held the overflow."
"Controllers?"
"Both the primary PLC and the Triconex SIS are flashed back to verified golden images from cold storage. The 2oo3 vote is whole again, the 0x7A4F override is gone, DB10 is clean on both the primary and the standby, and the key-switches are back in RUN/PROTECT."
"Root cause?"
"One adversary, six moves: a leaked DNS query behind an open proxy, a lying HMI, a bought-off safety vote, a rung that didn't exist, a pump that spoke Manchester, and a standby one sync away from inheriting all of it."

The sun comes up over Blackwood Reservoir. On the wall monitors, T-101 settles at a smooth, real five metres. The forensic dossier is signed and sealed - and this time the numbers on the screen are the truth.
